messages:
carla: FYI - customer (Org: fintech-x) filed a P1: sudden spike in tail latency and intermittent 502/503s after they pinned region=eu-central.
alex: Can you paste the error snippets or correlation id? Any change in request headers/region param?
carla: They sent this: 
`error: upstream_read_timeout, request_id=req_9832b4, route=generate`
Says they see requests routed to us-east and latencies ~800-1200ms.
jordan: That's odd — routing should honor region param. Did they use `region` or `preferred_region`? We had a recent change that treats `preferred_region` as soft hint.
maya: +1, we shipped a fallthrough change last week for routing where unavailable region triggers spillover to any compatible region. Could be hitting capacity in eu-central and falling back to us-east.
carla: Customer insists they explicitly set `region=eu-central` in the SDK call. Their headers: `X-Redwood-Region: eu-central` and `Authorization: Bearer sk-***`.
alex: Can you repro with their org header? Try curl with same key and region header.
carla: Repro steps I ran: 
1) `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-org-fintech" -H "X-Redwood-Region: eu-central" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":5}'`
2) Observe `200` occasionally but lots of `502` and high latency when it hits us-east.
opsbot: autoscale event: eu-central pool at 95% GPU utilization, queue_depth=120, backlog_spillover_triggered=true
jordan: That explains it — eu-central hitting capacity and our spillover policy currently routes overflow to the lowest-cost region (us-east) unless a strict pin is configured. Customer expected hard pin.
maya: There's a per-tenant flag `region_strict=true` that enforces hard pin and returns 429 if pinned region can't serve. Many customers don't enable it because it's brittle.
carla: Customer is unhappy; they think failover should not change latency characteristics and want clear behavior. Also billing got weird — they got charged at us-east rates for some tokens.
alex: Billing: we surface region in usage records. If requests run in us-east, billing uses us-east unit cost. Need to explain billing to customer and offer credit if unexpected.
jordan: Short-term mitigation: toggle their tenant to `region_strict=true` to force 429s instead of spillover. Will require config change in account service.
maya: Long-term: product triage — docs need to call out soft vs hard pin, and add a customer-visible header `X-Redwood-Executed-Region` in responses so callers can detect spillover.
carla: Customer asked for a reproducible log sample. I captured a trace: 
```
request_id=req_9832b4, incoming_region=eu-central, routed_region=us-east, route_reason=spillover_capacity, queue_time_ms=320, processing_ms=450
```
alex: Thanks. I'll open an infra ticket to investigate eu-central capacity oscillation and whether autoscaler underprovisioned due to recent kernel change.
opsbot: deploy-bot: rolled back autoscale config v2.14 -> v2.13 at 1769123500 due to instability
jordan: If autoscaler is flaky that's root cause. For now set `region_strict` for fintech-x and apply a one-off increase to their eu-central capacity (dedicated burst) to clear backlog.
carla: Done: set region_strict=true for fintech-x and applied +2 GPU burst to eu-central pool for their tenant. Notified customer and issued one-time credit for cross-region charges. Waiting for customer confirmation.
maya: Postmortem items: 1) Add `X-Redwood-Executed-Region` header, 2) Doc updates about spillover behavior and billing, 3) Autoscaler stability runbook, 4) Consider per-tenant spillover policy settings in Console UI.
carla: Customer confirmed latency normalizing and no more 502s. Closing after 24h validation. :relieved:
alex: Filed infra ticket INF-4593 and product ticket PRD-1287. Marking this thread as escalated -> eng-runtime.
carla: Thanks everyone. I'll add logs and the trace above to the support ticket and follow up tomorrow.
